chunks: From him, from several of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Dawud ibn al-Nu'man, from Abu Ayyub, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): We wish to hasten the departure, and it was the night of the first departure when I asked him, so at what time do we depart? He said to me: As for the second day, do not depart until the sun sets, and it was the night of the first departure. And as for the third day, when the sun has turned white (risen clearly), then depart, according to the word of Allah, Exalted and Mighty.

key_terms.عَلَى كِتَابِ اللَّهِ: According to the Book of Allah
key_terms.لَيْلَةُ النَّفْرِ: Night of departure (referring to the nights of 12th and 13th of Dhul-Hijjah)

ai.seo_question: What are the correct times for leaving Mina during Hajj according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfahani clarifies the distinct rulings for the two days of Tashriq, specifying that the first departure (12th) occurs after sunset while the second (13th) is permitted only after sunrise, thereby distinguishing between the obligatory stay and the permissible early exit. It underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on adhering to the precise temporal markers of the sun's position to fulfill the Quranic command of 'staying until the appointed time' (waqt al-ma'dud).
